- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.8) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly to avoid overshoot.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.4) or shows sharp reversal, model often underestimates; adjust upward to reflect potential rebound.
- Model frequently overreacts to recent spikes — especially if sentiment is neutral or mildly positive — leading to over-forecasted peaks; apply lagged smoothing or dampen momentum.
- In periods of high volatility or rapid price movement, model tends to overfit short-term noise; prioritize mean reversion toward historical range or 30-day moving average.
- If sentiment is flat or mixed (0.2–0.8), model often fails to capture mean reversion; use sentiment-weighted average of recent 7–14 day range as anchor.
- Forecast horizon 30d is prone to lagging: if sentiment is trending upward, delay peak forecast by 1–2 days; if downward, anticipate early dip.
- When sentiment shows strong reversal (e.g., from +0.8 to -0.4), model often misses the turn — adjust forecast to reflect 2–3 day lag in sentiment shift.
